text:
maria: FYI rolling BIOS batch in us-west2 just toggled the Secure Boot bit on ~28 nodes during the 02:00 maintenance window. Provisioner started failing hosts as expected. :eyes:

josh: ugh — are they stuck in the bootloader or failing attestation?

maria: attestation failures + some nodes drop to PXE fallback. Provisioning logs show `tpm: attestation: policy mismatch` then `boot-policy: requires-signed`.

ravi: spreading impact: two GPU pools (g4x-heavy and p3-batch) lost ~60% capacity for ~40m while autoscaler tried spinning new nodes. Cost spiked because fallback used on-demand in us-west2-b.

maria: exact. we routed traffic to other regions but latency-sensitive jobs started queuing. Queues hit backpressure and retries.

alaa: timeline? Can we roll a quick rollback of the BIOS flag?

maria: last firmware job was `fw-batch-2026-03-20-02` applied to 120 hosts. Only ~28 observed the reversion. Rollback plan: reapply signed baseline image with `-force-clear-secureboot` path. But that requires OOB console access for some nodes.

nelson: oncall, I've started running `oob-console scan --group=gpu-rack-usw2 --filter=secureboot=enabled` to list targets. Patch will need serial console flash on ~8 racks.

deploy-bot: Automated rollout paused for group `us-west2-gpu` (job id fw-batch-2026-03-20-02). Canary flagged: secure-boot-delta > threshold.

ravi: can we hot-fix by letting provisioner accept the changed flag temporarily? Maybe allow attestation fallback for this batch so we don't spin expensive on-demand.

sec-team: we prefer not to relax attestation; secure boot changes are high risk. If we accept machines with altered flags we need compensating mitigations (restrict network egress, revoke certs, rotate host keys).

maria: agreed — preference is to restore firmware state quickly instead. Ops plan: 1) pause the rollout (done) 2) schedule OOB console runs for the 28 nodes (nelson + infra runbook) 3) reflash the signed image and re-verify TPM PCRs 4) re-provision into pool and drain from on-demand fallback.

josh: for the nodes that can't be OOBed right away, can we create a temporary routing policy to send inference traffic to dedicated capacity with SLA credit? We should avoid failing customer jobs.

ravi: set `routing: prefer-dedicated` for affected tenant pools, and incrementally shift tasks over 15m windows. I'll handle autoscaler config.

nelson: running serial flashes now on rack 7, 9, 12 (approx ETA 14m per rack). Posting progress in this thread.

maria: log snippets for context: ```
Provisioner error: AttestationFailure: TPMPolicyMismatch(code=0x42)
BIOS fw job: fw-batch-2026-03-20-02, image: redwood-bios-1.4.3-signed
Affected nodes: host-usa-usw2-gpu-{0123..0149}
```

oncall-bot: Incident created INC-2026-0432: "us-west2 BIOS flag reversion -> provisioning backlog". Severity: P2.

sec-team: we'll need a short post-mortem item: investigate why the signed image re-applied the flag on subset. Possible causes: vendor rollback edge-case, corrupted metadata, or kernel-level reconfiguration during boot.

maria: once racks back online I'll run a verification job `verify-host-integrity` and attach the list. Also scheduling a targeted test of the firmware pipeline in staging to reproduce the delta.

ravi: cost note: on-demand fallback added ~ $5.2k over the 40m window. Logging chargeback to cost center infra-gpu.

josh: thanks team. please ping if you need extra hands for OOB. I'll coordinate with support to prioritize customer tickets that hit latency. :thumbsup:

nelson: rack 7 done, 6 nodes restored and rejoined the pool. provisioning success logs: `host-attachment: success`

maria: great — once all racks green I'll trigger a controlled re-run of the firmware pipeline with additional safety checks and a forced verify step.

sec-team: mark action items: 1) add pre-check for secure-boot bit diff in rollout 2) add automatic canary to OOB for first 5 hosts 3) vendor follow-up on signed-image behavior.

ravi: noted. updating runbook with temp mitigation (routing and cost center note).

maria: closing loop later with a short incident summary. Thanks everyone. :heart:
